title: Keep the main landmark at the top level
summary: The main landmark sits inside another landmark such as a region or aside. Move main out so it is a direct part of the page body.
problem: A <main> element (or role="main") is nested inside another landmark, such as <nav>, <aside>, <header> or a labeled <section>. The main landmark is meant to be a top-level landmark that marks the primary content of the page, not a part of something else.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users often list a page's landmarks and jump straight to the main content. When main is nested inside another landmark, that list shows a confusing hierarchy and it is harder to tell what is the primary content and what is the wrapper around it.
steps: Find the <main> element in your template and look at the elements around it. The scan result shows which one is the offending parent.
Remove the wrapping landmark (a <nav>, <aside>, <header>, labeled <section> or an element with a landmark role), or move <main> out of it so it is not a descendant of any other landmark.
If the wrapper is only there for layout, use a plain <div> instead, since a <div> is not a landmark.
Keep only one <main> on the page, and put the header, navigation and footer landmarks beside it, not around it.

whyItMatters: This is a best practice, not a WCAG failure. A clean landmark structure still helps people who navigate by landmarks find the primary content quickly, and it keeps your page template predictable for everyone who maintains it.
howToCheck: Open your browser's accessibility inspector or a landmarks extension and check that main appears at the top level of the landmark list, not indented under another landmark.
